However, we found no significant effect on the odds for pre‐eclampsia (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">OR</jats:styled-content> 1.308, 95% <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CI</jats:styled-content> 0.847-2.022).</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title><jats:p>In anticipation of more substantial population‐based data studies, in the Slovenian population, preventive treatment with low‐dose aspirin due to maternal characteristics and history of a pre‐existing medical condition is not beneficial for the prevention of pre‐eclampsia and can harm fetal growth.</jats:p></jats:sec>
